subject: Catalog onboarding: cloud marketplace listing requirements & exceptions
messages:
From: Nina Patel <nina.patel@cloudbazaar.co>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Ravi Menon <ravi.menon@cloudbazaar.co>
Date: 2026-03-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: steps for AWS/GCP marketplace listing + commercial exceptions

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the intro. CloudBazaar is prioritizing listing Redwood Inference in both AWS and GCP marketplaces this quarter to support our joint GTM. Two quick asks to make sure we can hit our internal procurement windows: 

1) A concise checklist of product/technical artifacts required for each marketplace (SaaS manifest, test endpoints, billing contract templates).
2) Any known product limitations or non-standard behaviors (e.g., token-level metering, streaming contract differences) that could require exception language in the marketplace contract.

We attached our onboarding questionnaire with initial answers — can your team annotate gaps?

Target timeline: public listing by April 20. Is that feasible from Redwood's side?

Appreciate your help,

— Nina
Head of Partnerships
CloudBazaar Inc.
Attachment: cloudbazaar-onboard-answers.pdf (PDF, 220KB)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Nina Patel <nina.patel@cloudbazaar.co>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-01T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: steps for AWS/GCP marketplace listing + commercial exceptions

Hi Nina — thanks for the questionnaire and timeline. Looping in Product (Camila) and Legal (Laura) so we can annotate and flag any exceptions. Quick notes from me: 

- Timeline: April 20 is aggressive but doable if we prioritize the AWS listing first and parallelize GCP. We will need product sign-off on a small set of integration tests and a short contract addendum for metering.
- Attachments: please also share a sandbox account or test API key so our infra team can validate the SaaS manifest behavior.

Camila — can you review the integration-specs-v2.xlsx I attached and call out any gaps by EOD Tuesday? Priyom, can infra confirm availability for a couple 2-hour validation windows next week? Laura, any initial legal redlines we should expect for marketplace terms?

I'll follow up with a suggested mutual action plan.

Thanks,
Jonas
Sr. Partnerships Manager
Redwood Inference
Attachment: aws-listing-checklist.pdf (PDF, 85KB)

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Nina Patel <nina.patel@cloudbazaar.co>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-02T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: steps for AWS/GCP marketplace listing + commercial exceptions

Thanks Jonas. I reviewed the questionnaire and the integration-specs-v2.xlsx (attached). High-level notes: 

- Tech gating items we need from CloudBazaar:
  * Sandbox tenant with 10k token/day limit for validation + sample dataset
  * API keys for non-prod endpoints and expected rate limits
  * Example streaming sessions (client -> server -> stream) we can replay
- Minimum product deliverables for marketplace listing:
  * SaaS manifest with redirect URIs and billing callback endpoints
  * Health check endpoints + sample responses for sequence-length 256/1024
  * Clear failure modes for fallback behavior when KV cache is cold
- Workarounds/exceptions: streaming meter variance — we meter on token completion; marketplace contracts often expect per-API-call pricing. That mismatch will need an addendum.

I can annotate the spreadsheet with line items and owners by tomorrow. Priyom — please propose two 2-hour slots (Tue/Wed) for infra validation.

-Camila
Product Manager, Integrations
Redwood Inference
Attachment: integration-specs-v2.xlsx (XLSX, 120KB)

From: Ravi Menon <ravi.menon@cloudbazaar.co>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Nina Patel <nina.patel@cloudbazaar.co>, AWS Marketplace Partner Manager <aws-mm@amazon.com>
Date: 2026-03-02T12:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: steps for AWS/GCP marketplace listing + commercial exceptions

Camila — great detail, thanks. Sandbox details attached; we've also added two example streaming sessions (jsonl) and a temporary test API key with restricted scope.

Notes from our side:
- We can accept an addendum that maps Redwood's token-level metering to a marketplace per-call invoice as long as the addendum includes a reconciliation formula (we can supply expected volume bands).
- Procurement flagged two potential exceptions:
  1) Data residency language for EU customers (CloudBazaar needs a contractual guarantee for region-bound logging).
  2) SLA credits — marketplace standard SLA calc differs from Redwood's Dedicated offering. They want to include a limited credit table in the listing.

We want to avoid delaying the April 20 target. If Redwood can confirm the metering reconciliation approach and provide the SaaS manifest by next Friday (2026-03-12), we can keep the schedule.

Thanks,
Ravi
Director, Strategic Partnerships
CloudBazaar Inc.
Attachment: sandbox-credentials.txt (TXT, 1KB)

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: Nina Patel <nina.patel@cloudbazaar.co>
Date: 2026-03-03T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: steps for AWS/GCP marketplace listing + commercial exceptions

Jonas/Camila — flagged a couple of legal items after an initial review: 

1) Metering addendum: we can draft a reconciliation clause that maps token counts to per-listing invoice lines, but Redwood requires visibility into aggregated token usage per account for audit. Will CloudBazaar accept a monthly usage report + a 30-day lookback right?

2) Data residency: Redwood's hosted offering supports region-specific logging but requires a signed DPA + customer choice of region. For marketplace listing, exception language must be explicit that region-bound logging is available on Dedicated/Private tiers, and hosted tier remains region-agnostic.

3) SLA credits: we prefer to keep marketplace listing with a “standard marketplace SLA” and present Redwood Dedicated as a premium with explicit credit tables rather than put multiple credit tiers into a single listing. If CloudBazaar insists, we need legal to agree to a short exhibit.

I'll attach a redline template for the addendum. Please review and note any commercial constraints.

— Laura
Associate General Counsel
Redwood Inference
Attachment: metering-addendum-template.docx (DOCX, 45KB)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Nina Patel <nina.patel@cloudbazaar.co>, Ravi Menon <ravi.menon@cloudbazaar.co>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, AWS Marketplace Partner Manager <aws-mm@amazon.com>
Date: 2026-03-03T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: steps for AWS/GCP marketplace listing + commercial exceptions

Thanks everyone — good progress. Quick summary / agreed next steps so we keep the April 20 target: 

- Product deliverables (Camila): finalized SaaS manifest + annotated integration-specs by 2026-03-12 (Camila)
- Infra validation (Priyom): two 2-hour validation slots next week — Priyom to confirm by 2026-03-04
- Legal (Laura): draft metering addendum and redline the DPA by 2026-03-06
- Commercial (Jonas): I'll draft a proposed reconciliation table for token -> per-call invoice bands by 2026-03-06 and share with CloudBazaar for feedback
- CloudBazaar: provide production SaaS manifest and confirm data residency requirements by 2026-03-12

If any of the internal owners foresee roadblocks (resource/time/technical), flag immediately so we can re-triage scope (AWS first, GCP follow).

Jonas
Sr. Partnerships Manager
Redwood Inference
